items.body: ““Ain’t nobody coming?” [Ali] said to Coltrane. “No, it’s just you and me.” “What are we playing? Is it fast? Is it slow?” “Whatever you want it to be. Come on. I’m going to ring some bells.”” -Quoted by Ben Ratliff in Coltrane: The Story of a Sound . John Coltrane’s sax-drums duo album with Rashied Ali, Interstellar Space , stands as a singular achievement in the history of free jazz. The duo’s restlessness, their commitment to musical exploration and the profound communication taking place between them would create a template that has animated the practice of free jazz to this day. Stef Gijssels, in his 2007 post on this website, wrote the following about that combination of instruments: “[It] offers a total freedom of interaction, but it's like poetry without rhyme, there is no comfort zone to fall back into, no safe haven, no safety net, it's swim or drown.” I think any jazz musicians wanting to tackle the drums/sax duo format must be very brave indeed, knowing that a comparison to Interstellar Space is almost inevitable. But they would also realize the freedom of unfettered expression that comes with it. And great musicians would view that as an opportunity to create something new, to engage in a genuinely novel musical conversation. Best of all, we get to eavesdrop on that conversation. I’ll always click on a drum/sax duo when I come across one on bandcamp. But I was especially happy to see this particular combo as I was familiar with both musicians and had very much appreciated earlier work of theirs. Both were in a trio album with Tim Berne, Poiēsis , one of the best albums of 2025. Drummer, percussionist Nava Dunkelman was also in a tremendous duo with violinist gabby fluke-mogul, titled Likht. Saxophonist Masayo Koketsu has a solo album, entirely on alto, called Ballade in which she plays jazz standards. She even covers Lover Man . (Seriously, I discovered this album in the course of writing this review and it’s exceptional. Do check it out.) The first track here, 初雷–hatsurai, begins with a thunderburst from Koketsu. Dunkelman matches her intensity. Google Translate tells me the title means First Thunder . Yup. I’ve listened to this album a bunch of times now and it still snaps my head back. These musicians are serious and they want your attention. Both musicians genuinely bring thunder on this track. There’s so much good music on this album, and what’s most impressive is the great variety of ideas to be found. The third track, 露の玉–tsuyu no tama, meaning Dewdrop Ball , is beautiful. Koketsu begins with lightning quick shards of notes with Dunkelman responding with bells. A reference to Interstellar Space ? Then there’s a brief bit of Ayler and then the musicians are off to explore more new ideas. The final and longest track 夕霧–yūgiri, meaning Evening Mist, is the best. It begins with plaintive playing from the saxophone with very light percussion. Then Koketsu’s playing gains in intensity and her lines become more complex. Dunkelman happily matches her and then takes over. Now she’s bringing the thunder and Koketsu again responds. Here, and throughout the album, these two musicians seem so in tune it’s a delight to listen to. Possibly the most surprising thing about this album is the first sentence of the liner notes: “Masayo Koketsu and Nava Dunkelman met for the first time in this studio session.” Veins of Rain by Masayo Koketsu, Nava Dunkelman Email This BlogThis! items.excerpt: 少年隊の植草克秀と音楽プロデューサーの井上ヨシマサによる新ユニットが始動。数々のヒットを生んできた井上の懐深い音楽性もさることながら、永遠の少年感を宿した植草のスターヴォイスも眩しい。少年隊への提供曲“PGF”の新アレンジでの再録、大人の青春ポップ“Forever Young”など、長年のファンならずとも親密さを抱かずにはいられないポップス集だ。

items.tags: ジャズ intoxicate 2026 August ジャズ ジャズ 坂田明 トリプルエッジ 坪口昌恭 早川岳晴 藤掛正隆 加藤崇之 船戸博史
items.excerpt: 1972年に山下洋輔トリオに加入し半世紀以上、80歳超えの巨人：坂田明はグローバルに活動し続ける。国内のみならず海外アーティストとの共演や共作、ジャズ～現代音楽～実験音楽など多岐にわたる様々なグループや名義で結成と解体を繰り返す坂田明 × トリプルエッジの4作目。本作は京都の老舗〈磔磔〉での2024年ライヴ実況録音盤。坂田明（アルトサクソフォン／クラリネット／ヴォーカル）を中心に坪口昌恭（ピアノ／シンセサイザー）、早川岳晴（エレクトリックベース）、藤掛正隆（ドラムス）という不動のカルテットに、スペシャルゲストとして加藤崇之（ギター）が4曲中3曲、地元・京都から船戸博史（コントラバス）が1曲で参加。即興とは演奏のみにあらず、会話であり対話。人との一期一会、血が通う怒濤のパフォーマンスを収録したアルバム。ええやんええやん。

items.excerpt: マックス・マーティンが絡んだ3曲を除いて彼の弟子のイリヤと本人がプロデュースし、ゲストなしで挑んだ8作目は、ダークなトーンで統一され、スピード・ガラージやシンセウェイヴで軽い変化をつけつつ、長らくメインストリーム・ポップの大きな柱になっている〈オルタナR&B〉が中心。ウィスパー声の多重録音が目立つ点も、“7 rings”や“34+35”と地続きにあるトラップ調のアプローチも含め、何となく『 thank u, next 』以降の総まとめ的に聴こえるのは、活動休止が発表された直後だから? 溌剌と歌い上げるアリアナも見たかったけど、それは次の楽しみにとっておきます。

items.excerpt: 目次 郷ひろみの変革のドキュメント 1986年、シネマティックな映像演出に宿ったプライド 1990年、ソロシンガーとして極限まで高めた本格的なショー 1994年、バラードシンガーとして頂点に再降臨した瞬間 〈Neo〉であり続けるスーパースターの進化の根源 1972年のデビューから半世紀以上、唯一無二の輝きで日本のエンターテインメントシーンを牽引し続ける郷ひろみ。昨年、70歳を迎えたが、今なお挑戦し続けるその姿は最新シングル“I’m Neo G”にもしっかりと刻まれていた。そんな国民的スターの進化の歴史を映し出すスペシャルボックス「GOLDEN STAGE HIROMI GO THE LIVE BOX 1986/1990/1994」が2026年11月25日（水）にリリースされる。当時30代だった郷ひろみが表現者としてその熱量と美学を注ぎ込んだコンサートの模様を、高画質で鮮やかに蘇らせた3枚組のBlu-ray／DVD作品だ。今回は、エディター／ライターの大窪由香にその歴史的価値と観るべきポイントを解説してもらった。 ＊Mikiki編集部

items.body:
TWICE’s TZUYU is bringing her voice to a crossover between Formula 1 and anime.

The singer joined Atlassian Williams F1 Team, DAN DA DAN and Sector Zero in Singapore on 9 October for a press conference centred on the collaboration’s upcoming theme song. Set for release in early 2027 alongside a new music video, the track will bring together the worlds of K-pop, motorsport and the supernatural anime series.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Bandwagon Asia | Music News • Asia Festivals & Artists (@bandwagonasia)

The project builds on Williams’ ongoing collaboration with DAN DA DAN, which has already included exclusive merchandise releases and an appearance at Anime Expo in Los Angeles.

“The energy in Singapore during race week is amazing, and I’m so happy I could share this moment with fans here,” TZUYU shared. “I hope everyone enjoys being introduced to Kokone at the Fan Zone. I can’t wait for you to hear the song next year.”

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Bandwagon Asia | Music News • Asia Festivals & Artists (@bandwagonasia)

Fans can get a first look at that world at the Atlassian Williams F1 Team Fan Zone at Marina Square. Running until 13 October, the space features special activations and new Singapore-exclusive merchandise showcasing Kokone, described as “an anomaly from TZUYU’s journey into the world of speed and supernatural”.

For Sector Zero’s Director, Lead Global Partnerships, Sayako Niimi, music was a natural next step for the collaboration.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Atlassian Williams F1 Team (@williamsf1team)

“I have always believed in the power of music to connect people across different cultures, languages, and generations,” she said. “So, when we built the collaboration with Williams and DAN DA DAN, the obvious next question was: ‘what does it sound like?’ When TZUYU came into our conversation, we had an answer.”

The forthcoming track adds to TZUYU’s work outside TWICE, following her solo debut with abouTZU in September 2024. Led by ‘Run Away’, the six-track mini-album reached No. 19 on the Billboard 200.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Bandwagon Asia | Music News • Asia Festivals & Artists (@bandwagonasia)

Fans can explore the collaboration in Singapore during Grand Prix week, with merchandise also available online through Sector Zero.

items.body:
Cao Yang (曹杨) is kicking off the new year with his first solo concert in Singapore.

The Chinese singer-songwriter and actor will bring his concert, Young “For Your Eyes Only” LIVE IN SINGAPORE, to the Resorts World Ballroom at Resorts World Sentosa on 2 January 2027, at 6 PM.

The concert takes its name from ‘For Your Eyes Only (仅你可见)’, a song Cao Yang wrote for his fans in 2025. Inspired by the connection he has built with listeners over the years, the show will revisit different chapters of his musical journey, spanning heartfelt ballads and more uplifting favourites.

“I look forward to sharing songs from different chapters of my musical journey - from heartfelt ballads to uplifting favourites - through a live experience filled with music, stories and surprises,” Cao Yang shared.

Fans may recognise Cao Yang from his appearances on The Next Singer (下一战歌手) and Magic Melody (魔力歌先生). His recent releases include ‘May I Shine Like A Firefly (愿若萤火)’, featured on the soundtrack of Chinese drama Against the Current (兰香如故), and ‘A Poetic Rendition of You (如诗一般的形容妳)’, composed by Jay Chou with lyrics by Vincent Fang.

The Singapore date follows two concert tours that have taken him to cities including Beijing, Shanghai, Taipei, and Kuala Lumpur. His upcoming Mandarin-language show will run for approximately 90 minutes.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by 曹楊Young (@young.cy1211)

Tickets will be available through priority sales from 13 October, 10 AM, followed by general sales on 15 October, 10 AM.

Priority sales: Damai, MAISEAT, and BookMyShow Singapore

General sales: SISTIC and Ticketmaster Singapore

Standard tickets: S$68, S$98, S$118, S$138, and S$158

VIP package: S$238, including a concert ticket, an autographed photocard, a limited-edition tote bag, and a photo opportunity with Cao Yang in groups of four

All ticket prices exclude ticketing service fees and handling charges. VIP purchases are limited to four tickets per transaction.

For fans planning a stay, limited two-night hotel packages at Hotel Ora or The Laurus start from S$1,245 nett for two guests. These include concert tickets, daily breakfast, and admission to Universal Studios Singapore and Singapore Oceanarium, for stays from 1 to 3 January 2027.

Visit the official concert page for tickets and package details.

items.body: As I already had the privilege to write a feature about the posthumously released album Stellar Regions on this blog, i want to stretch this even a bit further. Here, I take a look at the period to follow, which eventually and fatally turned out to be the last five months in John Coltrane’s life. My focus is on the production of music in this final stage, as far it has been recorded and released, rather than John’s personal or health condition. On 15 February 1967, John had recorded the tracks eventually released as Stellar Regions in 1995 (see my earlier feature) with the quartet. One week later, on 22 February 1967, he returned with Rashied Ali for a saxophone – drums duo session, eventually to be released as Interstellar Space (see Gary Chapin‘s feature on this album). On 07 March 1967, in another session with the quartet again, he recorded two tracks, as far as we know, Ogunde and Number One . Ogunde is, first of all, a relatively short piece at a few seconds over 3 ½ minutes. A noticeable parallel to Stellar Regions , where the title track and Iris have approximately the same length and concise structure. The track takes its title presumably from an afro-brazilean folk song „Ogundu Varere“, rougly translated as a prayer to the gods. John occupied himself with spiritual traditions especially from Africa. John uses his forceful, cry-like late saxophone sound, overblowing his instrument, which gives an emotional urgence to the piece. The theme starts with a solemn, hmyn-like melody, but breaks out in free, atonal outbursts, before it fades away. In summary, John condenses the intensity of his (at that time) usually half-hour long live improvisations into less than a handful of minutes (but see below, what happened live). At some time in spring (David S. Wild confirmed in the liner notes for Stellar Regions that this track was not recorded on 15 February, so the actual recording date remains unknown), John must have recorded To Be , where he plays flute and is rejoined by Pharoah Sanders on piccolo flute. He shows a very calm, introspective and meditative side here. At over 16 minutes playing time, this track feels like a spiritual retreat. The two flutes give it an airy, almost floating mood. Alice Coltrane’s flowing piano style provides a mystic, harp-like cushion. Rashied Ali on drums and Jimmy Garrison on bass keep it calm and subdued. All together, the piece lacks a trditional jazz pulse, even leaves traditional jazz structures completely and makes a profound structural switch towards a meditative, open-end spiritual incantation. It stands as one of the most explicit artifacts of the creative partnership between John and Alice at that final stage and already mirrors the „cosmic jazz“ landscapes that Alice would pioneer on her own in the years to follow in her landmark solo releases ( Universal Consciousness , Journey in Satchidananda). Not to forget about Pharoah Sanders (Karma). Also unknown is the exact recording date for the piece titled Expression in spring 1967 with the quartet, which later lended its title to the album. 23 April 1967 is the date of the last live recording, The Olatunji Concert. This performance, originally recorded for a radio broadcast, is featured by Fotis Nikolakopoulos on this blog, so see there. With due respect to Fotis, I will limit myself here to the absolutely striking contrast between the live version of Ogunde and the studio version. Performed live, it swells to 28 minutes playing time. The studio recording’s tight and condensed structure is only preserved in the theme at the beginning to which it returns only at the very end. In between, it gets overwhelmed by a storm-like wave of pure energy. After the introduction of the melody as theme, the structure collapses completely in a ritual storm. A dense, polyrhythmic vortex is unchained in Rashied Ali’s drumming. Alice Coltrane plays cascade-like runs on the piano. On saxophone, Pharoah Sanders adds his bone-rattling, ecstatic overblowing cries. Yes, the quartet has been expanded here. Pharoah Sanders is back at it on the second saxophone. Two additional percussionists joined in, Algie DeWitt and Jumma Santos. The last ever live gig came at Baltimore’s Famous Ballroom on May 7, 1967. No audio recording of that performance is known to exist. On 17 May 1967, exactly two months before John’s death, a sextet met for a last studio recording. The master tapes have been lost or at least unissued so two tracks with the titles None Other and Kaleidoscope have been unreleased so far and do not even appear on retrospective compilations. With the recorded material, a last studio record was conceived during John’s lifetime. It was given the title Expression . John was actively involved in the production and met with Bob Thiele. On side 1, it had Ogunde as the opening track (the studio version, as above, of course). Track #2 was To Be with John and Pharoah Sanders on flutes (as above). At over 16 minutes, it was the longest track, making up for nearly half of the original album’s playing time, and the only track on the album in which Pharoah Sanders made an appearance. Side 2 opened with the majestic ballad Offering , the only track chosen from the 15 February session, thus making it the only track on the posthumous album Stellar Regions (see there) that had been released before and had an original title. Hank Shteamer has just featured this track prominently in the New York Times and put it into the larger context of spiritual jazz, for which a piece like Offering „would seem like a perfect prototype“ (Hank Shteamer, Spiritual Jazz Has Turned Cozy. John Coltrane Demanded More. New York Times, September 18, 2026). The original album closed with the title track Expression, John‘s last studio recording to ever be released. In the later CD release only, Number O ne, recorded on the same day as Ogunde , was added as a bonus track (the track, however, had been released for the first time in a 1978 compilation album). Obviously, the most recent recording session of May 1967 was not considered in the process at all (at that time, the tapes at least should still have been around, I guess?). John reportedly selected the four tracks for the original album release and their exact sequence himself. On Friday, 14 July 1967, three days before his death, he met Bob Thiele, handed the master tapes over to him and finally authorised the title and the release of the album, but expressed his opposition against liner notes. Expression , as John Coltrane’s final statement, was released in September 1967, two months after his death, containing John‘s chronologically last audible studio recordings and being the first posthumous release of his music. items.album: Corners
items.artist: Enrico Rava Fearless Five with Joe Lovano
items.tags: jazz,avant-garde,improvisation
items.excerpt: Label: ECM Records, 2026 Personnel - Enrico Rava: trumpet; Joe Lovano: tenor saxophone, tarogato; Matteo Paggi: trombone; Francesco Diodati: guitar; Francesco Ponticelli: bass; Evita Pollidoro: drums, vocals. Illustrious Italian trumpeter and composer Enrico Rava, a longtime force on the European jazz scene, returns with his Fearless Five ensemble, welcoming guest saxophonist Joe Lovano, a powerhouse improviser who had collaborated with the bandleader on the live recording Roma (ECM, 2019). All
items.body: Label: ECM Records, 2026 Personnel - Enrico Rava: trumpet; Joe Lovano: tenor saxophone, tarogato; Matteo Paggi: trombone; Francesco Diodati: guitar; Francesco Ponticelli: bass; Evita Pollidoro: drums, vocals. Illustrious Italian trumpeter and composer Enrico Rava, a longtime force on the European jazz scene, returns with his Fearless Five ensemble, welcoming guest saxophonist Joe Lovano, a powerhouse improviser who had collaborated with the bandleader on the live recording Roma (ECM, 2019). All members of the quintet contribute compositions, trusting the bandleader's candidly investigative approach that opposes rigid perceptions. Rava's " Certi Angoli Segreti ", an exceptionally beautiful tune first recorded in 1998, gracefully materializes with beautiful color shades. Francesco Diodati's guitar gives it a particular touch, later soloing with motivic ability and acerbic distortion; Francesco Ponticelli's dynamic bass builds a solid foundation with drummer Evita Polidoro; Lovano's storytelling comes with delightful details; trombonist Matteo Paggi's expressions are grounded and exploratory; and Rava excels in his improvisational fluctuations—sometimes angular and outside, other times hypnotically flowing and distinctively melodic. Rava brings two other previously recorded pieces: " Hitchcock at the Beach ", whose balladic feeling and original beauty are preserved despite emerging here most as a collaborative voice-trumpet meditation; and the exciting " Bowery Dance ", which evokes Rava's New York years with an electrified intro, authoritative bass double-stops, and a crisp backbeat. Lovano and Rava improvise with fire, rejoicing in unison lines in support of their declarations. Lovano is credited with a couple of distinct compositions. The open-ended " Sun Rava " is full of possibilities, incorporating sharp staccato blows, buoyant swing impulses, and clever pedal points, also featuring improvised dialogues between Rava and Paggi, and then Diodati and Lovano, before the saxophonist rambles freely over the bass-and-drums bedrock. " Tone, Shape, and Colours ", a free improvisation based on a riff by Lovano, brings the horn players together in lively conversation. If the rhythm section kicks into high gear on Lovano's pieces, it eases into the softer lyrical flow of Diodati's " Sin Peso ", a burnished ballad suggesting a bolero feel, and Polidoro's " Le Mie Gambe ", which, unfolding in 3/4, features the drummer as a vocalist of surprising intensity. Since the early '70s, Rava—who turned 87 in August—has led a series of highly rewarding albums, and Corners is no exception. Favorite Tracks: 01 - Certi Angoli Segreti ► 06 - Tune, Shape, and Colours ► 08 - Bowery Dance

items.excerpt: “好きすぎて滅!”が今年を象徴するヒットに育つなか、“アイドルパワー”以降の配信曲などを束ねたミニ・アルバムが登場です。MUTEKI DEAD SNAKE × 浅野尚志によるラテン歌謡のリード曲“時空超えてユニバース”をはじめ、ロッキンなギターも力強いoni作編曲の“Don’t Let Me Down”、陽気な友情ソング“You!Joy!Parade!”など破竹の勢いを反映したアッパーな痛快曲だらけ!
